sentences.en: Good afternoon everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家下午好。

sentences.en: Well, with some of you about to go out on field work it's timely that in this afternoon's session I'll be sharing some ideas about the reasons why groups of whales and dolphins sometimes swim ashore from the sea right onto the beach and, most often, die in what are known as 'mass strandings'.
sentences.zh: 嗯，鉴于你们中的一些人即将开展野外工作，今天下午的课程适时地分享一些关于鲸类和海豚群体有时会从海里游向岸边、直接冲上沙滩并最终死亡的原因，这种现象被称为‘集体搁浅’。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, this type of event is a frequent occurrence in some of the locations that you'll be travelling to, where sometimes the tide goes out suddenly, confusing the animals.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这类事件在你们将前往的一些地点频繁发生，有时潮水会突然退去，使这些动物感到困惑。

sentences.en: However, there are many other theories about the causes of mass strandings.
sentences.zh: 然而，关于集体搁浅成因还有许多其他理论。

sentences.en: The first is that the behaviour is linked to parasites.
sentences.zh: 第一种理论认为该行为与寄生虫有关。

sentences.en: It's often found that stranded animals were infested with large numbers of parasites.
sentences.zh: 人们常发现搁浅动物体内寄生着大量寄生虫。

sentences.en: For instance, a type of worm is commonly found in the ears of dead whales.
sentences.zh: 例如，一种蠕虫常被发现在死亡鲸鱼的耳部。

sentences.en: Since marine animals rely heavily on their hearing to navigate, this type of infestation has the potential to be very harmful.
sentences.zh: 由于海洋动物高度依赖听觉进行导航，此类耳部寄生可能造成严重危害。

sentences.en: Another theory is related to toxins, or poisons.
sentences.zh: 另一种理论则与毒素或毒物有关。

sentences.en: These have also been found to contribute to the death of many marine animals.
sentences.zh: 这些毒素也被发现会导致许多海洋动物死亡。

sentences.en: Many toxins, as I'm sure you're aware, originate from plants, or animals.
sentences.zh: 正如你们所知，许多毒素源自植物或动物。

sentences.en: The whale ingests these toxins in its normal feeding behaviour but whether these poisons directly or indirectly lead to stranding and death, seems to depend upon the toxin involved.
sentences.zh: 鲸鱼在日常摄食过程中摄入这些毒素，但这些毒物是否直接或间接导致搁浅及死亡，似乎取决于具体毒素种类。

sentences.en: In 1988, for example, fourteen humpback whales examined after stranding along the beaches of Cape Cod were found to have been poisoned after eating tuna that contained saxitoxin, the same toxin that can be fatal in humans.
sentences.zh: 例如，1988年，在科德角海滩搁浅后接受检查的十四头座头鲸，被发现因食用含有石房蛤毒素（saxitoxin）的金枪鱼而中毒——这种毒素对人类同样可能致命。

sentences.en: Alternatively, it has also been suggested that some animals strand accidentally by following their prey ashore in the confusion of the chase.
sentences.zh: 另一种观点认为，某些动物是在追逐猎物时因混乱而意外搁浅。

sentences.en: In 1995 David Thurston monitored pilot whales that beached after following squid ashore.
sentences.zh: 1995年，大卫·瑟斯顿曾监测过一群因追随鱿鱼上岸而搁浅的领航鲸。

sentences.en: However, this idea does not seem to hold true for the majority of mass stranding because examination of the animals' stomach contents reveal that most had not been feeding as they stranded.
sentences.zh: 然而，这一观点似乎并不适用于大多数集体搁浅事件，因为对搁浅动物胃内容物的检查显示，它们在搁浅时大多并未进食。

sentences.en: There are also some new theories which link strandings to humans.
sentences.zh: 还有一些新理论将搁浅现象与人类活动联系起来。

sentences.en: A growing concern is that loud noises in the ocean cause strandings.
sentences.zh: 日益令人担忧的是，海洋中的巨大噪音会导致搁浅。

sentences.en: Noises such as those caused by military exercises are of particular concern and have been pinpointed as the cause of some strandings of late.
sentences.zh: 诸如军事演习所产生的噪音尤其令人关注，并已被确定为近期部分搁浅事件的诱因。

sentences.en: One of these, a mass stranding of whales in 2000 in the Bahamas coincided closely with experiments using a new submarine detection system.
sentences.zh: 例如，2000年巴哈马发生的鲸类集体搁浅事件，就与一项新型潜艇探测系统试验时间高度重合。

sentences.en: There were several factors that made this stranding stand out as different from previous strandings.
sentences.zh: 这次搁浅事件存在若干显著区别于以往搁浅事件的因素。

sentences.en: This led researchers to look for a new cause.
sentences.zh: 这促使研究人员寻找新的致因。

sentences.en: For one, all the stranded animals were healthy.
sentences.zh: 首先，所有搁浅动物均身体健康。

sentences.en: In addition, the animals were spread out along 38 kilometres of coast, whereas it's more common for the animals to be found in a group when mass strandings occur.
sentences.zh: 此外，这些动物分散在长达38公里的海岸线上，而集体搁浅时动物通常聚集在一起。

sentences.en: A final theory is related to group behaviour, and suggests that sea mammals cannot distinguish between sick and healthy leaders and will follow sick leaders, even to an inevitable death.
sentences.zh: 最后一种理论涉及群体行为，认为海洋哺乳动物无法分辨患病与健康的首领，因而会跟随患病首领行动，甚至走向必然的死亡。

sentences.en: This is a particularly interesting theory since the whales that are thought to be most social - the toothed whales - are the group that strand the most frequently.
sentences.zh: 这一理论尤为引人兴趣，因为被认为社会性最强的鲸类——齿鲸——恰恰是搁浅频率最高的群体。

sentences.zh: www.TopSage.com 录音稿 EV 该理论还得到2002年一次海豚搁浅事件证据的支持。

sentences.en: Exarination3- 189) the dead animals revealed that apart from the leader, all the others had been healthy at the time of their death.
sentences.zh: 检查（第3页-189页）显示，除首领外，其余死亡个体在死亡时均身体健康。

sentences.zh: www.TopSage.com 然而，若缺乏统一且一致的理论，我们几乎无法针对这一现象采取任何有效措施，只能在力所能及时尽力救助搁浅动物。

sentences.en: Stranding networks have been established around the world to aid in rescuing animals and collecting samples from those that could not be helped. recommend John Connor's Marine Mammals Ashore as an excellent starting point if you're interested in finding out more about these networks, or establishing one yourself.
sentences.zh: 全球已建立搁浅救助网络，以协助营救搁浅动物，并采集那些未能获救个体的样本。若你想进一步了解这些网络，或有意自行建立，强烈推荐约翰·康纳所著《搁浅的海洋哺乳动物》（Marine Mammals Ashore）作为极佳的入门读物。
